fact: ID Tech Wire reports Mauritania launched the Houwiyeti digital identity app giving access to government e-services, with biometric login to the e-services portal demonstrated in the March 2023 pilot.
source_slug: 2024-08-15 Mauritania Launches Digital ID for e-Services, Built on TECH5 Platform (Houwiyeti)

fact: The tax directorate (DGI) states taxpayers can declare and pay taxes online through its STT system and consult their tax file through its teleservices portal.

Ecofin Agency, citing Mauritanian authorities, reports that services including driver's licence applications, the road traffic digital system, criminal record issuance, vehicle registration documents and loss certificates for official documents have already been digitised, and that national electricity company services were integrated into the "Khdamati" digital platform.
The government launched on 4 April 2025 the 'Mes services' portal and app with two services, online company creation and investment-code accreditation requests.
Minister told the National Assembly that several digital services are now available to citizens; no count or portal named.
A Mauritanian official claims about forty transactional online services, of nearly 900 targeted.

On 12 May 2026 the national health solidarity fund (CNASS) launched its digital services on the national portal Khidmaty, offering online affiliation, secure online contribution payment and file tracking, with EU support.
The energy minister said SOMELEC's subscription services, including viewing bills, are available through the government portal Khidmaty, fully electronically, from 17 December 2025.
Ministers launched the online university registration service Tasjil on the national public services portal Khidmaty, where students enter data, pay fees by e-wallet and receive their certificate.

The Council of Ministers on 30 October 2024 adopted a draft decree setting the management and access rules of the KHADAMATI public services portal, meant to ease citizens' access to administrative services.

Decree 2024-154 fixes how the Khidmaty digital portal for public services is managed and accessed, with a management cell at the digital ministry and each sub-platform created by joint ministerial order.

An op-ed says citizens can request documents and services remotely through Houwiyeti and track requests, and that the criminal record, digitised in March 2025, can be obtained remotely via Houwiyeti and the Khadamati platform.
